text:
Alex Chen: Heads up — p99 on the latency pane jumped from ~420ms -> ~1.8s right after a quota fallback at ~11:23. Route: /v1/generate (service: gen-eu). Anyone else seeing this?

quota-bot: AUTO: quota-fallback triggered for tenant=acme-inc at 2025-08-12T11:23:07Z — routing to fallback pool 'dedicated-low-priority' (weight=1.0)

Maia Singh: interesting — fallback pool uses a slower GPU profile and the model-variant is quantized-8. That could explain tail-only increases. p50 barely moved? :thinking:

Devon Park: confirm — p50 ~430ms -> 480ms, p95 ~610ms -> 650ms, p99 jumped big. Can we get a per-host / per-endpoint breakdown? Wondering if console rollup merged tdigest from different sample_origins incorrectly.

Sophie Ramos: can you paste the console query you ran? want to check sample_origin tag and whether the rollup used tdigest merging or raw samples.

Alex Chen: here's the query I ran in console:
```
SELECT pctile(latency_ms, [50,95,99]) as p FROM latency WHERE route='/v1/generate' AND env='prod' AND window=5m GROUP BY endpoint_tag
```
Result snapshot I copied:
- endpoint gen-eu-1: p50=440ms p95=620ms p99=1800ms
- endpoint gen-eu-2: p50=420ms p95=610ms p99=460ms

Maia Singh: that looks like one host in gen-eu-1 saw a long tail. Check routing policy — fallback weight might have shifted traffic unevenly to a small subset of hosts.

Devon Park: also check sample_origin. Console sometimes tags samples as sample_origin=proxy when fallback/redirect happens; if we blindly merge tdigest sketches from different origins without preserving counts/weights we can blow up p99.

Sophie Ramos: @Alex can you share recent rollout weights? and can eng-runtime confirm KV cache warm state? Cold KV or queueing could blow up tail.

Alex Chen: rollout weights (screenshot uploaded to thread). gen-eu-1 received +30% of fallback traffic during window. KV hits looked okay in traces but we saw queue depth spike. logs pasted: 
```
2025-08-12T11:22:58Z [gen-eu-1] queue_len=120 avg_latency_ms=190
2025-08-12T11:23:03Z [gen-eu-1] queue_len=560 avg_latency_ms=430 p99_latency_ms=1820
```

obs-bot: Metric alert: queue_len gen-eu-1 > 500 for 2m (alert id: Q-2025-876).

Maia Singh: OK — working hypothesis: quota fallback caused routing shift -> one host overloaded -> p99 blowup -> console rollup shows endpoint-level p99 large while p50 stays similar. Two asks: 1) Should console surface sample_origin counts by default? 2) Should routing engine prevent shifting >20% of fallback traffic onto a single host during sudden reroutes?

Devon Park: +1 on both. UX side: add a small pill on the latency pane for "sample origin" with counts. Backend: implement a "fallback spread" policy to evenly distribute fallback traffic across the pool.

Sophie Ramos: I'll file an eng-platform ticket for the console UX and tag eng-runtime for the routing policy fix. Short-term: annotate dashboards when quota-fallback events coincide with p99 spikes so support can triage faster.

Alex Chen: +1 — annotation will help triage. Also add a runbook note: when p99 >> p95, check for concurrent fallback events and per-host queue_len.

Devon Park: I'll prototype a query to show per-host tdigest vs raw-sample p99 to prove merge artifacts. will post results here soon. :hammer_and_wrench:

Maia Singh: thanks — if we can correlate timing to rollout weight change ops can revert faster.

Sophie Ramos: Filed: PLAT-1229 console: show sample_origin pill + annotate fallback events (owner: Sophie Ramos).

Alex Chen: thanks everyone. keeping thread open — will update when devon posts the query.

Devon Park: posted gist with the prototype query: https://gist.github.com/devon/abcdef — it computes raw sample counts and compares tdigest-merged p99 vs raw p99 per host. early finding: merged p99 can be overstated when a host has a tiny sample_count but an extreme tail. i'll drop numbers later.

Alex Chen: great, useful. once we have numbers we can decide whether to change rollup to "count-normalized" merging or just show raw-cohort pills.

Sophie Ramos: agreed. closing for now but ping me if new spikes show up.
